footer.tagline: Discover Nuwara Eliya like a local. Plan a trip that feels like yours.
footer.description: Curated journeys through misty tea country, high-elevation botanical trails and quiet colonial architecture in Sri Lanka’s historic hill station.
footer.copyright: © {year} Nuwara Insider. Dedicated to authentic Ceylon highland exploration.

hero.tagline: Misty tea hills, colonial charm, and cool mountain air. Honest guidance from locals — completely free.

featuredExperiences.heading: Things worth doing here
featuredExperiences.subheading: Not a checklist. A considered set of ways to spend your time in the hill country.

items.title: Horton Plains & World's End
items.description: Walk the plateau at dawn and reach the escarpment edge where the land drops 880 metres into the valley below. Best in the dry season when the mist clears by mid-morning.
items.alt: Open plateau of Horton Plains at first light

items.title: Pedro Tea Estate
items.description: Follow the leaf from bush to cup inside one of the oldest working estates in the hill country. The factory tour is unhurried and the people who run it have been here for generations.
items.alt: Terraced tea rows on a hill-country estate

items.title: Gregory Lake at First Light
items.description: A quiet walk along the colonial-era bund before the town wakes. The lake sits perfectly still in the early morning, the surrounding hills reflected in it without distortion.
items.alt: Still lake surrounded by green hills at dawn

popularTripIdeas.heading: Trips that already make sense
popularTripIdeas.subheading: Whole itineraries, not a list of things to sort through yourself. Pick the one closest to your trip and adjust from there.

items.title: A Week in the Hills
items.description: The unhurried version. Enough time to actually settle into the pace of the hill country — tea estates in the morning, the plateau at dawn, long lunches, and evenings that end early because the air turns cold. Built for people who would rather do four things well than ten things quickly.
items.alt: Winding road through misty tea plantation hills

items.title: 3 Days as a Couple
items.description: A short, quiet trip built around slow mornings and one good view. Less itinerary, more mood.

items.title: The Long Weekend
items.description: For when you can only get away for two days but still want it to feel like a proper trip, not a rushed detour.
items.alt: Aerial view of rolling green hills under a cloudy sky

seasonalGuide.heading: Best Time to Visit
seasonalGuide.intro: Nuwara Eliya sits at 1,868m — it stays cool year-round, but the dry season (December to March) is when the hills are at their most magical.

seasons.title: The April Season
seasons.description: Nuwara Eliya at its fullest — horse racing, motor racing, and the town in bloom.

seasons.title: Dry Season
seasons.description: The clearest skies of the year. Best odds for uninterrupted views from Horton Plains.

seasons.title: Misty Mornings
seasons.description: Fog rolls through the tea hills before sunrise. Quieter, slower, and photogenic.

seasons.title: Shoulder Season
seasons.description: Fewer travelers, lower rates, and still good weather for getting around.

whyTrustUs.heading: Travel designed for the high country.
whyTrustUs.intro: Highland Sri Lanka rewards deliberate travelers who know when the mist falls and how mountain distances actually feel.

pillars.title: Elevation & Pacing
pillars.description: At nearly 1,900 meters, mountain roads turn 20 kilometers into a 60-minute journey. We structure schedules to protect you from car fatigue.

pillars.title: Microclimate Timing
pillars.description: Nuwara Eliya shifts from sparkling blue morning skies to drifting mist by early afternoon. We orient walks to catch panoramic views before the cloud rolls in.

pillars.title: Authentic Artisanry
pillars.description: Skip the souvenir-factory gift halls. We point you to working tea estates, gardens and heritage places run by people who know them well.

pillars.title: Curation Over Quantity
pillars.description: No generic lists of 100 roadside stalls. Every recommendation is handpicked, regularly reviewed, and matched to how you like to travel.

weather.title: The Weather Reality: Mist, Showers & Sunshine Windows
weather.description: Mornings are often bright, then cloud drifts in by midday and showers can follow in the afternoon. Do the important thing early and keep a waterproof layer in your bag.

transport.title: Getting Up the Hill: Train, Car or Bus
transport.description: The hill-country train is the scenic way up to Nanu Oya, a private car is the most flexible, and the public bus is the cheapest. Each suits a different kind of traveler.

seasons.title: Best Seasons: Horton Plains and the Dry Months
seasons.description: December to March is the most reliable window for clear mornings at World's End. April is the busiest month, and mid-year is quieter, wetter and very green.

aboutPage.subheading: Nuwara Insider is a digital local travel consultant for Nuwara Eliya. It helps independent travelers decide where to go, in what order and when, without selling them a hotel or a tour.

pacing.title: Mountain roads are slow
pacing.text: Distances look short on a map and take much longer on winding hill roads. Plans here have fewer stops and more time between them.

mornings.title: Mornings come first
mornings.text: Mornings are usually the clearest part of the day, and mist tends to build later. Each place has a best time of day, and the planner orders every day around it. It also flags the wetter months.

advice.title: Advice, not sales
advice.text: There is nothing to book, reserve or pay for on this site. It is a place to decide and plan, then go.

estimates.title: Estimates, said plainly
estimates.text: Drive times and visit lengths are estimates, not promises. We say so on every plan and refine them as we learn more.

tripIdeas.label: Trip ideas
tripIdeas.text: Ready-made routes you can open in the planner and change to suit you.

guides.label: Travel guides
guides.text: Practical reading on weather, getting there, what to pack and more.

planner.heading: A plan built from fixed rules
planner.intro: Answer a few questions and the planner builds a day-by-day itinerary. It follows set rules, not AI, so the same answers always give the same plan, and a shared link shows exactly what you saw.

pace.title: Your pace sets the day
pace.text: A relaxed pace means fewer stops and later starts. An active pace fits more in and can begin at dawn.

party.title: Who is travelling matters
party.text: Demanding outings are left out for families and for travelers who want a relaxed pace, and the plan tells you what was left out and why.

transit.title: How you get around changes the plan
transit.text: Far places such as Horton Plains need a car, so they are left out if you travel by train and local transport. Drive times run longer on that route and when you drive yourself.

month.title: The month of your trip counts
month.text: May to September are treated as the wetter months, so rain-sensitive stops are ranked lower and the plan says so.

saved.title: Places you save stay in
saved.text: Anything you save is always included. If it cannot fit, the plan tells you instead of quietly dropping it.

cta.heading: Start with a plan, or just ask.
cta.text: Answer a few questions to get a day-by-day itinerary, or send a question to a local first.

privacyPage.title: Privacy
privacyPage.intro: This page explains, in plain language, what Nuwara Insider keeps about you and what it does not. The short version is that we ask for very little.
summary: Your planner answers and saved places stay in your own browser.
A question you send through Ask an Insider reaches us by email, and we use it only to answer you.
We do not use analytics or advertising trackers on this site.
There are no accounts, and nothing on this site takes a payment.

sections.title: What you send us
blocks: The only time you send us information is when you use Ask an Insider. The form asks for:
your question and the topic it is about
an email address, a WhatsApp number, or both, so we can reply
your travel dates, if you choose to give them
any of three optional notes about your trip: an infant or toddler, motion sickness on winding roads, or a slower walking pace
Please do not include anything more sensitive than you need to. The optional notes are there so we can answer well, and you can leave them blank.

sections.title: What stays on your device
blocks: The trip planner and the saved-places list work without an account. Your answers, your planner draft and the places you save are kept in your browser's local storage on your own device. We do not receive them and cannot see them. Clearing your browser data removes them.

When you open a finished itinerary, the answers that produced it are written into the link itself, such as the number of days and your interests. If you share that link, the person who opens it can see those answers. The link does not contain your name or contact details.

sections.title: How we use it
blocks: We use what you send through Ask an Insider only to read your question and reply to you. Your message reaches us as an email. We do not add you to a mailing list, and we do not sell your details.
The planner and the saved list never leave your browser, so there is nothing for us to use there.

sections.title: Other companies involved
blocks: A few outside services touch the site, and you should know about them:
Email: your question travels through our email service so that it can reach us.
Hosting: the server that delivers this site may keep standard logs, such as the pages requested and the visitor's IP address, for security and to keep the site running.

Photos: some photographs on this site are currently loaded directly from Unsplash and Google servers, so your browser contacts those companies when a page with those photos opens. We are replacing them with our own photographs.
Maps: a place's location opens in Google Maps only if you click the link. Nothing is sent to Google until you do.

sections.title: Cookies and tracking
blocks: We do not use analytics, advertising or tracking cookies, and we do not build a profile of you.
The site may remember your language choice in a small cookie so that it opens in the right language. It does not identify you.

sections.title: Keeping and deleting
blocks: We keep your question and our reply only as long as needed to answer you and follow up. If you would like them deleted, tell us through Ask an Insider and we will delete them.
Because planner answers and saved places are stored only on your device, you can delete them yourself by clearing this site's data in your browser settings.

sections.title: Contact
blocks: Questions about this page, or a request to see or delete what you have sent us, can go through Ask an Insider. Choose the topic Something else.

contact.heading: Questions about this page?
contact.text: Send them through Ask an Insider and a person will read them.

termsPage.title: Terms of use
termsPage.intro: These terms explain what you can expect from Nuwara Insider and what we ask of you. They are short on purpose.
summary: This site gives travel advice. It does not sell, book or arrange anything.
Times, distances and conditions are estimates, so check before you go.
Advice from Ask an Insider is given in good faith. It is not professional advice.
Outdoor travel carries risk, and the decisions on the day remain yours.

sections.title: What this site is
blocks: Nuwara Insider is a guide and planner for visitors to Nuwara Eliya in Sri Lanka. It offers descriptions of places, ready-made trip ideas, travel guides, a trip planner and a way to ask a question. It is for your personal trip planning.

sections.title: No bookings or payments
blocks: You cannot book, reserve or pay for anything on this site. The times in a plan are suggestions about when a place suits you, not reservations. We do not arrange transport, stays, guides or tickets.
If you decide to use a driver, hotel, guide or any other service, that arrangement is between you and that provider.

sections.title: Plans and estimates
blocks: Itineraries are built from fixed rules and the answers you give. Drive times, visit lengths and heights are estimates. Weather, road conditions, opening hours, entry fees and rules at parks and estates can change without notice, so please check them before you travel.
Mountain weather in particular can change quickly. We cannot promise clear skies, open roads or access to any place on a given day.

sections.title: Your safety and your choices
blocks: Walking, hiking, early starts and mountain roads carry real risk. You are responsible for judging whether an outing suits your health, fitness, group and the conditions on the day. Follow the instructions of park, estate and local staff.
Where a place is marked as demanding, take that seriously. Turning back is always a good plan.

sections.title: Ask an Insider
blocks: Replies are local advice given in good faith. They are not medical, legal or other professional advice, and they depend on what you tell us and on conditions that change.
There is no fixed response time, and we may decline to answer a question. How we handle what you send is described in the privacy page.

sections.title: Links and content
blocks: Some links lead to other websites, such as Google Maps. We do not control those sites and are not responsible for them.

The text and design of this site belong to Nuwara Insider, and some photographs belong to their owners. You are welcome to use the site and share links to it. Please ask us before republishing whole pages or photographs.
Please do not misuse the site, or send it anything unlawful, abusive or misleading. We may block misuse.

sections.title: Limits and changes
blocks: We take care to keep the information here accurate, but we cannot promise that it is complete or up to date. To the extent the law allows, we are not responsible for losses that come from relying on it. Nothing in these terms takes away rights you have under the law.
We may change the site or these terms. The date at the top shows when this page last changed. Questions can go through Ask an Insider.

contact.text: Send them through Ask an Insider and a person will read them.
